chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abu Khadija, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Even if the servant were inside a rock, God would bring him his sustenance — so be moderate in your seeking.'

key_terms.أَجْمِلُوا فِي الطَّلَبِ: Be moderate/graceful in your seeking — a command to seek livelihood with dignity, without greed or anxiety
key_terms.الْعَبْد: The servant/slave — used here to denote any human being in their relation of total dependence on God
key_terms.رِزْق: Sustenance, provision — in Islamic theology, each person's rizq is decreed by God and includes all of life's blessings

ai.seo_question: Does Islam guarantee that God will provide sustenance regardless of circumstances?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches that God's provision (rizq) is guaranteed for every person regardless of circumstances, even if one were sealed inside a stone. The phrase 'be moderate in seeking' (ajmilu fi al-talab) was a standard Imami counsel against anxious over-exertion in livelihood pursuit, reminding believers that the responsibility for provision lies with God, not human striving alone.
word_analysis: He would surely bring to him
